title: How to Read a Local Market Report
description: A number becomes useful when you understand its source, time period and scope.

sections.title: Start with the geography
sections.body: Check the exact area covered and whether the report reflects a city, county, ZIP code or subdivision. These are not interchangeable.

sections.title: Look at the reporting period
sections.body: A monthly figure, year-to-date figure and rolling average answer different questions. Check publication dates and note whether data may be revised.

sections.title: Understand the measure
sections.body: Median sale price is the middle sale in a defined group; it is not the value of a particular home. Days on market and inventory measures depend on reporting definitions.

sections.title: Bring the question back to your plan
sections.body: Broad trends provide context. A purchase or sale still needs property-specific research and a strategy that reflects your circumstances.
